observations:
Torah 116 (LM2) contains no explicit bechina language of the form 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y.' The teaching is structured as a sustained analogy (כְּמוֹ כֵן): Eretz Yisrael's paradox of physical ordinariness combined with extreme inner holiness is compared to the Tzaddik's paradox of appearing like all humans while being 'an entirely different matter.' The word 'בְּחִינוֹתֶיהָ' in paragraph 5 is a noun ('its dimensions/aspects'), not a relational equation. 

For a new package to be proposed, the spec requires 3 or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. This criterion is not met: the text has no bechina declarations at all, and the analogy between Eretz Yisrael and the Tzaddik is an analogical comparison, not an ontological equation ('A is a bechina of B'). 

The teaching's two-domain structure — (1) hidden holiness: Eretz Yisrael / Tzaddik / Ish Kasher / Emunah; (2) perceptual error: physical sight / mistake of external form — is fully captured in the additions.json gap analysis as candidate nodes for future dataset entry. These domains, while coherent and analytically meaningful, cannot be formalized as new bechina packages because they are not grounded in any bechina declarations in the source text. The relational structure of this Torah is analogical and eitza-directional (belief/faith → discernment of holiness), not bechina-based.
